sentence_of_record: SPLIT-FOLLOWUPS (2026-09-23, zero calls; data steward, independently recomputed by the adversarial reviewer): the tree of record bareq512_s42 is snapshot 20260909_212117, which was LLM-labelled and rubric-induced. Induction withheld the pool of record by exact text, so 28 p2dca questions still had a norm-v1 twin, with its key, in a leaf's induction corpus, and 26 twin texts were in the leaf labelling prompts; route (b) therefore applies to the RUBRIC-512 family. The STACK-v2 anchor rubrics are not bareq512's: the ladder induced them from the frozen tree's centroids on 2026-09-07, and 14 norm-v1 twins of judged questions (0 exact) sit in their corpora. The link hazard never reached a scorer: the checker, the Kotlin arena and k_reconcile read the judged eval row or the category, which agrees on all 3,445, and its 54 mismatches are 31 construction copies (D1's 31), 20 sentinels and 3 others, caused by a last-writer-wins text map. The union tree and its six grafts ran no labelling and no induction.

plain_description.what: Audits whether any judged readout accidentally used the linked MMLU-Pro dataset row instead of the evaluation row that was actually judged. It also traces text twins into tree labelling and rubric-writing inputs. No calls.
plain_description.why: A mismatch between the judged question and the scored row would corrupt accuracy and agreement numbers.
plain_description.information: No hazard means scorers are safe. A hazard would require re-scoring. Result: done. The link hazard never reached a scorer (scorers read the judged row, which agrees on all 3,445). But the tree of record was LLM-labelled and rubric-induced, and 28 judged questions had a near-twin in a leaf's rubric-writing corpus. Scorers were spot-checked, not exhaustively.
